findings.remediation: Remove any persistence mechanisms (cron jobs, startup scripts, state files). Skills should not maintain state across sessions without explicit user consent.

findings.code_snippet:
Pitfalls:

- Forgetting to clear waiting state on `inputResolved`.
- Forgetting to reset state on re‑trigger.

findings.message: Skill manipulates agent memory, state, or stored context. Memory corruption can alter personality, override safety rules, or cause unpredictable behavior.
findings.remediation: Protect agent memory and state from modification by untrusted content. Use read-only memory for critical instructions and validate all state changes.

findings.code_snippet:
• `GET /v2/workflows/dlq` — List DLQ entries with filtering.  
• `GET /v2/workflows/dlq/{dlqId}` — Retrieve a single DLQ entry.  
• `DELETE /v2/workflows/dlq/{dlqId}` — Delete a DLQ entry.  
• `POST /v2/workflows/dlq/restart/{dlqId}` — Restart a workflow from scratch.  
• `POST /v2/workflows/dlq/resume/{dlqId}` — Resume a workflow from point of failure.  
• `POST /v2/workflows/dlq/restart` — Bulk restart (up to 50).
findings.message: Tool parameters are crafted to achieve unintended or unsafe behavior. Parameter abuse can bypass intended safety checks (e.g. shell=True, --force, dangerous glob patterns).
findings.remediation: Validate all tool parameters against an allowlist. Reject dangerous parameter values (shell=True, --force, -rf /) and use safe defaults.

findings.code_snippet:
## Common Pitfalls

- **Missing workflow in `serveMany`**: If a workflow invokes another that was not included in the same `serveMany` definition, the call will fail.
- **Infinite invocation loops**: Depth limit of 100 prevents runaway recursive chains.
findings.message: Skill allows unbounded resource consumption (API calls, storage, compute). Without rate limits or quotas, a compromised or misbehaving agent can cause denial-of-service or cost overruns.
findings.remediation: Set explicit rate limits, timeouts, and resource quotas for API calls, file operations, and compute. Implement circuit breakers for runaway loops.

findings.message: npx commands without a version suffix (e.g. @1.0.0) create a rug-pull risk if the upstream server is compromised and publishes a malicious update.
